data.title: 265 Topics to Master AI Engineering (and the 6-Week Order I'd Learn Them In)
data.description: 265 AI engineering topics from roadmap.sh's AI Engineer (189) and AI Agents (100) roadmaps, deduped, plus the 6-week order to learn them and what to build each week.
data.label: Roadmap

data.title: I Knitted My GitHub Into a Christmas Sweater (and You Can Make Yours)
data.description: Type a GitHub username and your last year of contributions gets knitted into a Christmas jumper, shown in six real-looking product photos. How the canvas knitting works, and how a Codex photo shoot became a shop that knits anyone's graph into the wool.
data.label: Build

data.title: Made of Things: My Name Where Every Letter Turns Into Something From My Life
data.description: Type motion where each letter of my name turns into a glossy 3D thing: my laptop, a rocket for the YC startups, my coffee and a 3D emoji of me, made with Codex. Six modes (lens, pop, shuffle, wave, sticker, burst), one spring per letter, no libraries.
data.label: Build

data.title: ASCII Reels in Python: an Eye That Zooms Into a Heart, Roses Rising and a Golden-Angle Sunflower
data.description: How I took apart a viral ASCII eye reel and rebuilt it in Python with NumPy and ffmpeg, then made two more: roses that grow and bloom, and a sunflower drawn with the golden angle.
data.label: Build

data.title: Exploded: A Shoe Store Where the Scroll Takes the Shoe Apart
data.description: How I built a running shoe page that comes apart into its five parts as you scroll, each with a callout and a price, and lets you recolour any part before it snaps back together. All from one Codex picture and six Codex edits.
data.label: Build

data.title: Front Row: A Fashion Store Where the Scroll Walks the Show
data.description: How I built a fashion store where you sit at the end of the catwalk: scroll and the looks walk toward you, the one that stops at the front is for sale and the cameras go off. One Codex catwalk, one Codex model, seven Codex outfit edits and a little perspective maths.
data.label: Build

data.title: Movement: A Watch Store Where the Scroll Is Time
data.description: How I built a watch page where the hands are set to your time and tick like a real movement, and scrolling winds them forward while the dial clears to show the gears. A Codex watch with no hands, three Codex edits, drawn hands and a loupe.
data.label: Build

data.title: Paint Job: A Sofa You Re-Upholster by Dropping a Swatch on It
data.description: How I built a furniture store where you drag a fabric swatch onto the sofa and the new fabric soaks in from where it lands. Seven Codex photos of one room, a mask worked out from where they differ, and one WebGL shader. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Receipt: A Grocery Shop That Prints Itself as You Scroll
data.description: How I built a corner grocer whose whole shop is one thermal receipt coming out of a printer as you scroll: a Codex printer, sixteen Codex groceries dithered to thermal dots, and a page where only the paper moves. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Scent Cloud: A Perfume Store Where You Can See the Spray
data.description: How I built a perfume page where holding the bottle sprays a cloud of particles that drifts on a breeze, gathers into the names of the notes and fades the way a scent does, top notes first. Codex bottles and about a hundred lines of canvas.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Claw: A Toy Store Where You Win the Toys
data.description: How I built a toy store whose hero is a claw machine: a Codex photo of an empty cabinet, ten Codex toys cut out with macOS Vision, Matter.js bodies shaped like each toy, and a claw that holds on (sometimes). Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Tank: A Skincare Store Under Water
data.description: How I built a skincare store where the products drift in a tank of water: stir it with the pointer, click a bottle and it rises through the bubbles with its ingredients floating up beside it. Codex photos, a 2D canvas and one WebGL water pass.
data.label: Build

data.title: Throw It On: A Streetwear Store Where the Clothes Snap Onto the Model
data.description: How I built a store where the clothes float round the model and snap onto her when you fling them. One Codex model, one Codex edit per piece, and a prep script that turns each edit into a layer so any top goes with any bottom.
data.label: Build

data.title: Unboxing: A Headphone Store Whose Hero Is the Delivery
data.description: How I built a product page you open like a parcel: drag across the tape to slice it, the flaps open from the cut, and you pull the headphones up out of the tissue. A Codex box, the same box opened, and the headphones in three colours.
data.label: Build

data.title: Mission: NASA's Perseverance Rover, Flown to Mars by Your Scroll
data.description: How I turned NASA's public Perseverance 3D model into a scroll-driven CAD drawing: designed, assembled, launched on an Atlas V, landed in Jezero and driven. Three.js, hidden lines, prompts inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Toran: Five Indian Doorways You Can Walk Through
data.description: How I built /lab/toran: Codex-generated doorway lintels, Matter.js strands made of each region's welcome in its own script, and bells that ring when you swipe.
data.label: Build

data.title: Try On: A Bag Store Where One Model Wears Every Bag
data.description: How I built a luxury bag store where you pick a bag, it flies onto the model and the new look ripples out from where she wears it. Codex for the model and the bags, macOS Vision for the cut-outs, one WebGL shader. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Entangled: Particles That Flow Between Two Browser Windows
data.description: Open the page in two windows and their particle orbs pull on each other, joined by streams that cross the gap and follow the windows as you drag them. No server: BroadcastChannel, screen coordinates and Three.js. Code and prompt inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: I Redesigned My GitHub Profile README With Animated SVG Cards
data.description: My GitHub README now matches my site: a hero with an ASCII portrait that prints in, three world tiles, a monthly chart and a blue contribution graph. All SVG, refreshed daily.
data.label: Build

data.title: Agent Crews: 48 Cursors, a Queue and a Crew for Every Block
data.description: My page that builds itself, scaled up: 48 named agent cursors wait in a queue, every block gets a crew, the headline is carried in letter by letter and a reviewer sends work back. Code and prompt inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Agent Sheet: A Portfolio as a Spreadsheet My Agents Fill In
data.description: My Reel numbers as a spreadsheet that ten named agent cursors fill in at once: titles typed, stats pulled, a formula dragged down, a heat map and a chart. Real data, real HTML, code and prompt inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: How a Gaming Chip Built a $5 Trillion Empire: The True Story of Nvidia and CUDA
data.description: Nvidia put a feature nobody used into every chip it sold, and Wall Street ignored it for years. Then two gaming cards in a Toronto bedroom changed everything.
data.label: Case study

data.title: A Robot Hero That Follows Your Cursor, Made From One AI Video
data.description: How I made a hero section where a retro robot turns its head to follow your cursor: a Media.io image, one Kling video clip, transparent frames and a bit of eye tracking.
data.label: Build

data.title: Agents at Work: A Page That Builds Itself, Block by Block
data.description: How I made a page that a swarm of named agent cursors builds live: a blue marquee, a grey skeleton, then the real thing, typed headlines and pixel fills. Code and prompt inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Claude 101: How I Made the Matrix Desk Animation
data.description: The 3x3 grid reveal edit from my reel, broken down frame by frame. Exact timings, the flash recipe, how to shoot it, and the prompt I used to get Claude to edit it for me.
data.label: Build

data.title: Wet Paint: A Gallery Where Each Painting Soaks In Over the Last
data.description: How I made a full-screen gallery of the world's best views as oil paintings, where each new one soaks in from the top like wet paint: Codex for the paintings, one canvas, a noise field, a blurred wash and drips. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Floating Phones: an A24-Style 3D iPhone Carousel for My Reels
data.description: How I built a Three.js carousel of floating iPhones that play my most watched Reels, with a foldable intro, a Codex poster to zoom through and a hand-drawn hover loop. Code and prompts inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: 6 Ways to Put Your GitHub Graph on Your Portfolio (Animated, With Real Data)
data.description: Pull your real GitHub contribution calendar with one GraphQL query and animate it six ways on canvas: the grid, a 3D skyline of commits, a weekly pulse, a year clock, your streak and a terminal. Code and a prompt inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: Buildings That Draw Themselves: Line Art That Soaks Into an Image, Like Heron's Hero
data.description: How I made a full-screen carousel of buildings that draw line by line, then fill in like ink: Codex for the drawings, OpenCV to trace their lines, SVG for the draw and a canvas dissolve. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: I Turned Myself Into 66,000 Dots: a WebGL Point Cloud Portrait With a Real Loader
data.description: How I built a point cloud bust of myself in Three.js: one photo, Codex for a clay version of me, Higgsfield to turn it into 3D, dots baked into one binary file, a loader that is the real download, and a cursor that is a light. Prompts and code inside.
data.label: Build

data.title: I turned myself into a 3D character and explored the Taj Mahal
data.description: Avatar to rigged 3D character in Tripo, monuments from one line of text, and a playable world built with Opus 5.5. Every prompt, step and code snippet, plus free Tripo credits.
data.label: Build

data.title: I Put My WHOOP Data on My Portfolio: the WHOOP API, Explained by Building a Live Dashboard
data.description: How I built /fitness from the WHOOP API: OAuth with rotating refresh tokens, the data model, webhooks, rate limits, the heartbeat intro, and the full prompt.
data.label: Build

data.title: Turn Anything into an Apple-Style 3D Website (I Did It with a Bowl of Ramen)
data.description: The full workflow: Tripo for the 3D models, Opus 5.5 for the code. Prompts, code snippets and the free credits link.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Prompt Behind My Vox-Style Portfolio Page: Paper, Highlighter and a Camera That Reads It for You
data.description: How I turned my portfolio into a scroll-driven Vox explainer: Codex generated the paper, tape, marker and halftone assets, and one CSS variable per chapter runs every animation.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: The Prompt Behind My Second Hero: A Deck of Reels Dealt Into a Fan That Lifts Into a Turning Wheel
data.description: A copy-pasteable prompt and the code concepts behind the Deal hero: Reel cards dealt face down, flipped into a fan while the loader counts, then lifted into a wheel of playing videos rising out of the clouds.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: The Prompt Behind My Homepage: A Loader That Deals Cards Into a Ring, Then Opens Into the 3D Carousel Hero
data.description: A copy-pasteable prompt and the code concepts behind avivashishta.com: Reel cards dealt around a small tilted ring while a counter loads, then the same cards expand into the full-screen carousel. One pose function, no handoff, no second scene.
data.label: Prompt

data.description: At My Desk is my actual desk setup rebuilt as a 3D website: lamps you can switch on and off, a monitor and laptop you can type on, a globe, a plant to water and a phone that becomes a focus timer. data.description: A scroll-driven infinite zoom through 15 nested illustrations, from a bookshop into a book, a ship, a snow globe and out to a star, then back again. How the hand-written WebGL shader, the slow-down at each world, the loader and the ink-reveal type work, what I removed, and what still has seams.

data.description: All 209 free AI projects from awesome-llm-apps (140K stars) and ai-engineering-hub (38K stars), with a checked link for each: RAG, agents, MCP, voice, fine-tuning, sorted from beginner to advanced, plus the 10 I would build first.

Three ways to start, the four phases I'd do first for an AI app developer job, what to ship after each, and which capstone to build.

Setup, India job boards to point it at, and how to use it well when only 5.9% of Indian tech postings are entry level.

data.description: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol launched the same day. Pricing, context windows and benchmarks from the official pages, why the launch benchmarks can't be compared, the cheap GPT-6 Luna option, and a 20-minute test to pick your own default. Checked 24 September 2026.

data.title: Cosmo: The Replit Prompt I Used to Polish a 3D Robot Companion (and What Actually Shipped)
data.description: A single-file Three.js robot you can boop, pet, throw and upset, with 11 moods, two hidden meters, spring physics, synthesised sound and a MediaPipe webcam Mirror mode. The full Replit polish prompt, which parts shipped and which were cut, and the tail-clipping and emote-timing fixes.

data.title: YC Summer 2027 Internships: Where to Apply (and What to Do From India)
data.description: Y Combinator's Summer 2027 internship page is live. The official page, three more boards that track YC and startup intern roles, India AI internship listings you can apply to now, and how to write an application a small startup will actually read. Checked 24 September 2026.
data.label: Career

data.title: 8 GitHub Repos That Make Claude Code 10x Better
data.description: Eight open-source repos that change how Claude Code behaves: a skills framework, an agent harness optimizer, tool-output trimming, git worktree management, a parallel-agent fleet runner, cross-tool memory, an anti-over-engineering ruleset, and an answer-first output skill. Star counts verified 23 September 2026.
data.label: Build

data.title: One Desk Photo, Three AI Clips: Building a Cinematic Agent Command Center With Replit's Video Generator
data.description: How one rear-view desk photo became a 24-second cinematic sequence of AI agent terminals using Replit's video generator: why the second clip changed direction instead of polishing the first, why a named palette and a 'do not include' list beat mood words, how chaining clips from the last frame keeps the scene continuous, the generator's limits, and three copy-pasteable prompts.
data.label: Build

data.title: What 2027 Interviews Will Actually Ask You
data.description: Fifteen questions software engineering interviews are moving toward in 2027 — working alongside an AI assistant, reading unfamiliar code, defending your own architecture decisions, and explaining AI systems — with what to prepare for each, and a four-week plan. Sourced from Google's AI-assisted pilot, Meta's AI-enabled format, HackerRank's interview modes and CoderPad's 2026 hiring survey.
data.label: Career

data.title: ASCII Studio: Images, 3D Models and a Live Webcam Turned Into Editable ASCII
data.description: A browser studio that converts images, GLB/OBJ models and a live camera feed into ASCII you can edit in real time. Why every source has to collapse into one converter, why density is a cell size and not a character count, why monospace cells are not square, how the three exports are three different problems, and the full Replit Agent brief.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build a pear.no-Style Scroll-Scrubbed Cinematic Site on Replit (WebP Frames, Not Video)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Replit Agent prompt for a single-page cinematic WebGL site in the style of pear.no — one sticky stage 60 viewports tall, one normalized progress number, scroll-scrubbed WebP frame sequences instead of seeking a video, a halving-stride loader that never shows a blank frame, six shader transitions, and an asset pipeline that generates motion first and decomposes it with ffmpeg.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build a Premium Property Site on Replit (Scroll as the Medium)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Replit Agent prompt for a luxury property site where scroll is the medium — a masked arch preloader, a sticky hero dive, a word-spacing spread, a horizontal track sized from its own content, clip-path curtains, a page that clips into a card at the footer, and six reveal primitives that each have a mirrored exit.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: Making Rain Splash Off Your Body in Real Time
data.description: A webcam effect where rain falls and bursts the instant it touches your silhouette. The whole thing is a rising-edge test against a segmentation mask — plus three bugs, including one where heavier rain produced fewer splashes.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Design Language of Era Residence: Scroll as Choreography
data.description: A breakdown of era-residence.com: split-text reveals with matching exits, a different parallax per section built on sticky rather than pin, viewport-gated video, continuous theme swapping, and a logo whose spin speed tracks your scroll velocity.
data.label: Build

data.title: I Built a 3D Car Dealership Without Opening Blender
data.description: Generating every vehicle from a single photo with Tripo AI, then shipping it on the web: the file:// CORS wall, the over-compression mistake that ruined the meshes, weld() before simplify, a 164-part exploded view, and a refraction cursor shader.
data.label: Roadmap

data.title: Turning Your Webcam Into Liquid Metal With 400 Lines of Python
data.description: A real-time mercury/chrome webcam effect at 77 fps without TouchDesigner and without a GPU: a three-line wave equation, gradient-driven refraction, specular lighting from the same gradient, and a feedback loop that makes the image melt.
data.label: Build

data.title: I Built a Rubik’s Cube Solver in One HTML File with Claude (Three.js, a Layer-by-Layer Solver, and Photo Scanning)
data.description: Cube Lab is a single HTML file: a Three.js 3x3 you can drag-turn, a layer-by-layer solver written from scratch with IDDFS and conjugated generators, and a scanner that reads your real cube from six photos or your webcam.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build a Fake Old Computer on Replit (Beige Plastic, a CRT Screen, and Buttons That Actually Travel)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Replit Agent prompt for a skeuomorphic site where the whole page is one piece of 90s beige hardware — chunky bezel, green phosphor CRT with scanlines and bloom, a fake POST boot sequence, and knobs, switches and buttons that physically move.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: Pinch Time Travel: Scrubbing Video With Your Fingers in 300 Lines of Python
data.description: Spread your fingers and a timelapse runs forward; squeeze and it rewinds. How Avi Vashishta built a pinch-to-scrub video player with MediaPipe hand tracking and OpenCV — including the four bugs that only show up in front of a real camera.
data.label: Build

data.title: Top 5 Design Trends To Make Your Website 10x (Product and E-commerce, 2026)
data.description: Brand story before product, hyperrealism over AI minimalism, walkthroughs and trials instead of demo forms, Gen-Z-fication, and trust signals built for humans and AI shopping agents. Five design trends for product and e-commerce websites in 2026, with the numbers behind each one.
data.label: About

data.title: Motion Gallery: A 3D Painting Orb You Rotate With Your Hands (MediaPipe + React Three Fiber)
data.description: Thirteen famous paintings on a Fibonacci sphere you spin by pinching the air. The object-fit: cover maths for Three.js textures, pinch-and-drag and two-hand-zoom gesture handling with MediaPipe, an alpha WebGL canvas over a live webcam, and the CSS fallback for when there is no WebGL context.
data.label: Build

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build the Luma Floor Lamp Hero on Replit (A Brass Switch That Lights the Whole Page)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Replit Agent prompt for an editorial product hero on pure black — a photoreal floor lamp you switch on with a real brass inline switch, a halo behind the shade, a warm floor bounce, copy that dims when the room goes dark, and a pool of light that follows your cursor.
data.label: Prompt

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build Lumina, an Interactive Light Gallery on Replit (Pull-Chain Physics, Drag-to-Dim, Hold-to-Ignite)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Replit Agent prompt for a pure-black fullscreen gallery of three photoreal lamps, each turned on by a different physical mechanic — a Matter.js pull chain, a drag-to-dim paper lantern, and a hold-to-ignite neon tube. Edge-masked photos, procedural Web Audio, no sound files.

data.title: Turning Yourself Into Spider-Man in React (MediaPipe Pose → a Mixamo Rig in React Three Fiber)
data.description: A webcam, a 368 MB Spider-Man GLB and React Three Fiber: capture your empty room, walk back in, and the suit is standing where you are — your size, your pose, your fingers. The full retargeting maths and the five bugs that each looked like something else.

data.title: The Prompt I Used to Build Hook Lab in Emergent (20 Scored Instagram Hooks, Biased Toward What Already Worked)
data.description: A copy-pasteable Emergent prompt for a full-stack hook-writing app — 20 tagged and scored hooks per topic, a two-second red flag computed in code, caption generation with per-section regeneration, and a feedback loop that learns which hook formats actually perform on your account.

data.title: How I Built an Animated GitHub Profile README (ASCII Portrait + Neofetch Card + Live Contribution Graph)
